text:
maria: quick q — we need finalized inputs from HW partners for the cost model / marketplace listing + reserved/spot assumptions for next quarter. can each vendor confirm: reserved tiers & discounts, spot baseline (avg % capacity), regional caveats, marketplace listing credit structure, and standard lead times? deadline EOD Thu so we can lock the pricing deck.

nick_hw: sure — i can share our current sheet. TL;DR: 1yr reserved (commit) = ~30% off list, 3yr = ~45% off; marketplace listing can add a 4% promo credit we pass through. spot availability varies by region, avg 35% usable but with large swings during events (10–70%).

rachel_fin: maria — we need the normalized cost per GPU-hour after discounts (USD), plus an expected variance band for spot. finance will plug these into the unit economics model.

nick_hw: understood. sample numbers (effective after partner discount and marketplace credit):
```
region: us-west2
1yr reserved price (effective): $0.68 / GPU-hr
3yr reserved price (effective): $0.44 / GPU-hr
spot average (expected): $0.30 / GPU-hr (±40% variability)
marketplace promo pass-through: 4% credit applied to invoice
lead time for reserved capacity: 6–8 weeks provisioning on committed pool
```

anil_ops: clarify: when you say "provisioning on committed pool" is that soft-commit (can we scale out earlier) or hard pinned SKUs? also any zone-specific blacklist (we need this for routing fallbacks).

nick_hw: it's a soft-commit pool for dedicated partners — we can prioritize pinned capacity for you if you sign a PO + onboarding checklist. zones: ap-southeast has lower spot depth and occasional AZ maintenance windows — avoid as primary for latency-sensitive routes.

maria: lovely. tara_legal, any contract flags re: passing marketplace credit to customers vs Redwood margins?

tara_legal: main points: 1) marketplace credit is typically reflected on vendor invoice and can be passed to the customer if contract text allows; need explicit pass-through clause. 2) reserved discounts require minimum term language + early-termination terms. i'll draft a short addendum template we can reuse.

vendor-bot: uploaded: https://files.redwood.example/partners/nick_hw_costsheet_q2.csv (csv, 1 sheet)

rachel_fin: thanks — i'll ingest that and return normalized GPU-hour numbers by EOD Wed. maria — can you confirm whether marketplace promo should be modelled as direct discount or absorbed into go-to-market credits? affects margin calculus.

maria: model as direct discount to partners for the pricing deck. we will show an "after-credit" effective unit cost in the public-facing pricing annex; internal calcs should also keep a before-credit column.

anil_ops: one operational ask — please include expected preemption behavior for spot instances (grace period, typical reclaim window). critical for batching/parallelization planning.

nick_hw: spot reclaim: 2 minutes notice via signal, average reclamation window ~30s to 3m depending on region. we can expose preemption signal to your runtime.

maria: action items: 1) nick_hw to confirm final CSV + signed pass-through ok (nick) — due EOD Thu; 2) rachel to publish normalized numbers (EOD Wed); 3) tara to draft pass-through addendum (Fri); 4) anil to capture routing/zone constraints into the runtime config doc (next sprint).

maria: anything else? :eyes:

nick_hw: nope, i'll push an updated CSV with region breakdown and the 1/3yr ladder and cc tara.

rachel_fin: will run sample sensitivity and share a 2-slide summary for QBR.

tara_legal: will drop a short clause + checklist into the shared drive.

anil_ops: i'll open a small RFC on the runtime side to map the zone blacklist/priority pools.

maria: perfect — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
